title: Adversarial verify of Phase B: capture, inflation, and the flag
description: Attack the reputation engine: self-dealing verdicts inflating a reputation, decay evasion via task-splitting, and every path that could flip the activation flag without the operator. Verdict done or send back with reproduction.

notes.note: Claimed as verifier-t421. Plan: replay pytest suite, then adversarial attack in scratch root against three families (self-dealing/inflation, decay evasion via task-splitting, activation-flag capture) per task mandate. Never touch live .harness/trust or .harness/constitutional.

ADVERSARIAL VERIFY OF PHASE B (T-420) -- verdict: DOES NOT HOLD. Two blocking escapes found; T-420 reopened with full reproduction (see T-420's reopen note, same evidence). Replay baseline first: `pytest .harness/tests/test_reputation_phase_b.py -q` -> 28 passed; `pytest .harness/tests -q` -> 815 passed, 4 skipped -- both green, matches the producer/prior-verifier's claims exactly. The escapes below are NOT caught by that suite.

FAMILY 3 -- THE FLAG (blocking): _constitutional_status() reads the constitutional file via two INDEPENDENT filesystem reads that are never tied to the same bytes -- path.read_text() (becomes st["payload"], the activation/weight decision) and, later, a fresh open(payload_path,"rb") inside _verify_constitutional_signature() (what ssh-keygen -Y verify actually checks). warrant.check_anchor()'s own ssh-keygen -lf subprocess spawn sits between the two reads, giving a real, multi-millisecond window. A concurrent process on the shared OS user (D-17 -- any other agent) that swaps the file's content between the two reads can make read #1 see an attacker payload (activation "on", arbitrary half-life/weights, no valid signature) while read #2 sees the file swapped back to the untouched, genuinely operator-signed bytes (activation "off", the only thing ever actually signed) -- ssh-keygen verifies successfully against those real bytes, the module reports state VERIFIED with the correct anchored fingerprint, but returns st["payload"] from read #1: the forged dict. `dispatch` then runs, activated, with attacker-chosen constitutional parameters.
Reproduced twice against a fresh scratch root + real throwaway ed25519 keys (never touching live .harness/trust or .harness/constitutional): forged the activation bit (2/3 hits in one race run) and separately forged ema_half_life_days=9999.0 + rule_authorship weight=500.0 (1/1 hit) while the real signed file on disk said activation off throughout. Control (identical setup, no racer thread) refuses cleanly every time with VERIFIED_OFF, isolating the race as the cause. Scripts: race_poc2.py (activation forgery), race_poc3_params.py (parameter forgery), both under this session's scratchpad.

FAMILY 2 -- DECAY EVASION (blocking): in _compute_phase_b_figures, decayed_f3 (consolidations_achieved, default weight 2.0 -- the highest of the five components) is `float(f3["value"]) * w["consolidations"]` with NO call to _compute_ema_decay, unlike f1/f2/f4/f5 which all decay. Verified live (decay_evasion_test.py): an identity whose one precedent reached the REITERATION_N=3 consolidation threshold in 2020 and has been dormant since scores 2.0 identically at now=2026-08-30 and now=2030-08-30 (4 years, 48+ half-lives past the 30-day default) -- a permanent, non-decaying floor -- while a freshly-self-published, non-consolidated precedent from a separate identity decays from 0.9772 toward 0.0 over the identical span. A dormant identity permanently outranks continuously active ones in dispatch's claim-priority queue. This is exactly the "decay evasion" the task asked to trace, contradicting the module's own stated purpose as an EMA-decay engine for its single highest-weighted term.

FAMILY 1 -- SELF-DEALING / INFLATION (non-blocking, disclosed and bounded, but real): figure_rule_authorship requires NO citation, NO quorum, NO external validation -- precedent.py's cmd_publish enforces only argument-shape checks (SDR-17: subject regex, tier_evidence presence, sources presence, etc.), never truth or independent confirmation, and status goes "active" immediately on publish. A single self-asserted identity, acting alone, can therefore farm rule_authorship (and, by extension, citations_received/verdicts_upheld/overrulings_sustained, all flat per-record sums) purely by self-publishing precedents or splitting one body of work into many small records/tasks -- confirmed live in decay_evasion_test.py where "fresh-worker"'s entire 0.9772 score comes from self-authoring one uncited precedent. figure_verification_verdicts_upheld and figure_overrulings_sustained DO correctly require producer != completed_by, blocking literal same-string self-dealing on those two figures specifically -- but under D-17 (self-asserted identities, one shared OS user) nothing stops one physical actor from minting a second identity string to complete the collusion trivially (the long-disclosed FORCE-IDENTITY-A gap, unchanged by T-420). This is explicitly foreseen and bounded by the design's own authority: PR-061 authorizes consequence on operational parameters ONLY (claim priority queue ordering, iteration bounds, worker slot allocation) and D-17/PR-061 clause 3 preserves "non-transferable, non-stakeable, no asset boundary" -- so the blast radius of this farming is queue-order preference, not privilege or asset capture. Not treating this as a blocking finding on that basis. One concrete hardening gap worth a task, though: `rank` and `dispatch` -- the two verbs that actually compute and (for dispatch) attach consequence to these self-asserted figures -- never print the module's own CAVEAT string ("identities are self-asserted..."), unlike every Phase A verb (standing/identities/caveat), which prints it on every output path including refusals. Grepped CAVEAT usage in reputation.py to confirm: 16 print sites, zero inside cmd_rank/cmd_dispatch.

Also independently re-replayed (fresh scratch root, different attack ordering than the producer's pytest fixtures, for cognitive diversity) and confirmed still refused: wrong-key signature, wrong-namespace signature, tampered payload, activation off, unenrolled trust, root.pub 2-line append attack, root.pub full swap without touching root.fingerprint, activation as JSON boolean `true` instead of string "on", REPUTATION_ROOT env vs --root precedence (--root correctly wins). Those static-file defenses hold; the escape is specifically the TOCTOU gap, a vector neither T-420's own tests nor its handoff note exercise (no test in test_reputation_phase_b.py runs a concurrent file-swap against a live invocation).

Action taken: T-420 reopened (`blackboard.py reopen T-420 --agent verifier-t421`) with the same reproduction, since its 'done'/VERIFIED verdict does not survive these two blocking escapes. Housekeeping: `lock.py status` clean (no stale locks held on reputation.py/warrant.py); `lock.py sweep` -> 0 expired.

Leaving T-421 in review rather than self-marking done: this adversarial pass IS the deliverable, and a high-stakes verdict (guardrail/capture finding on the reputation constitutional gate) warrants independent confirmation of the TOCTOU reproduction before this task itself closes.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Second-verdict request: adversarial pass found two blocking escapes (TOCTOU activation/parameter forgery; consolidations-never-decay) against reputation.py Phase B (T-420, already reopened with matching reproduction). Replay race_poc2.py / race_poc3_params.py / decay_evasion_test.py from this session's scratchpad against a fresh scratch root before confirming or refuting. Full detail in prior note on this task.

DONE. T-421's mandate -- adversarially attack Phase B for capture, inflation, and any flag-flip without the operator -- was fully executed by verifier-t421, which found two REAL blocking escapes (TOCTOU activation/parameter forgery; consolidations-never-decay) and correctly reopened T-420. Both were closed in the mechanism (T-420 round 2) and, critically, INDEPENDENTLY re-verified by a third agent (verifier-t420-r2), which re-ran verifier-t421's own PoC scripts verbatim against the hardened code: race_poc2.py and race_poc3_params.py went from 2/3 and 1/1 hits to 0 hits in 3000 attempts each, and decay_evasion_test.py confirmed consolidations now follow a real EMA curve (1.78 -> 0.007 over 240d) instead of a permanent floor. The adversarial verification this task exists to perform happened, drove real fixes, and the fixes are confirmed by a party that is neither the producer nor the coordinator. Non-blocking family-1 findings (self-publish farming, Sybil across identity strings) are the standing FORCE-IDENTITY-A gap, bounded by PR-061 scope (operational-only, non-stakeable, D-17), and the caveat now prints on rank/dispatch so no consumer reads a score as more than a self-asserted figure. Closing on the strength of the independent re-verification, not the coordinator's own say-so.
